def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Recover the bottom-to-top stacking order of overlaid rectangular color frames.

    Input structure:
    - The background is one color, and every foreground color is a one-cell-thick rectangular frame.
    - Overlapping frame pixels show only the color of the frame that is highest at that location.

    Rule:
    - Reconstruct each frame as the border of the bounding box of its visible pixels.
    - At every cell covered by multiple reconstructed frames, the visible frame color is above the other frames covering that cell.
    - Return the unique bottom-to-top order of frame colors as a single-column grid.

    Key insight:
    The hidden parts of each frame do not need to be seen directly; the visible pixels reveal the full frame bbox, and overlap cells reveal the layer constraints.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    bg = int(get_bg(g))
    colors = colors_present(g, exclude={bg})
    assert colors, "input must contain foreground frames"

    frame_masks: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
    for color in colors:
        visible = g == color
        b = bbox(visible)
        assert b is not None, "each foreground color must be visible"
        mask = _frame_mask(g.shape, b)
        assert np.all(mask[visible]), "visible pixels must lie on their reconstructed frame border"
        frame_masks[color] = mask

    edges: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    h, w = g.shape
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            covering = [color for color in colors if frame_masks[color][r, c]]
            if len(covering) < 2:
                continue
            top = int(g[r, c])
            assert top in covering, "an overlap cell must show one of the frames covering it"
            for color in covering:
                if color != top:
                    edges.add((color, top))

    assert edges, "frames must overlap to determine their order"
    order = _unique_layer_order(colors, edges)
    return np.array(order, dtype=int).reshape(-1, 1)

def _frame_cells(r0, c0, r1, c1):
    """Return set of (r, c) for the 1-cell-thick border of a rectangle."""
    cells = set()
    for c in range(c0, c1 + 1):
        cells.add((r0, c))
        cells.add((r1, c))
    for r in range(r0 + 1, r1):
        cells.add((r, c0))
        cells.add((r, c1))
    return cells


def _sample_layer_order():
    n = random.choice(FRAME_COUNT_CHOICES)
    colors = random.sample(FRAME_COLORS, n)
    random.shuffle(colors)
    return colors


def _random_frame_size():
    fh = random.randint(*FRAME_HEIGHT_RANGE)
    fw = random.randint(*FRAME_WIDTH_RANGE)
    return fh, fw


def _place_first_frame():
    fh, fw = _random_frame_size()
    r0 = random.randint(0, GRID_HEIGHT - 1 - fh)
    c0 = random.randint(0, GRID_WIDTH - 1 - fw)
    return (r0, c0, r0 + fh, c0 + fw)


def _place_next_frame(prev, prior_cell_sets):
    """Sample one frame that crosses the previous frame and stays compatible with older frames."""
    pr0, pc0, pr1, pc1 = prev
    for _ in range(PLACEMENT_TRIES):
        fh, fw = _random_frame_size()
        r0 = random.randint(max(0, pr0 - fh + 1), min(GRID_HEIGHT - 1 - fh, pr1))
        c0 = random.randint(max(0, pc0 - fw + 1), min(GRID_WIDTH - 1 - fw, pc1))
        r1, c1 = r0 + fh, c0 + fw

        if r1 >= GRID_HEIGHT or c1 >= GRID_WIDTH:
            continue

        new_bb = (r0, c0, r1, c1)
        new_cells = _frame_cells(*new_bb)

        if len(new_cells & prior_cell_sets[-1]) not in REQUIRED_PREV_OVERLAPS:
            continue

        if any(len(new_cells & cells) not in ALLOWED_PRIOR_OVERLAPS for cells in prior_cell_sets[:-1]):
            continue

        return new_bb, new_cells
    return None


def _place_frame_stack(n):
    first = _place_first_frame()
    bboxes = [first]
    frame_cell_sets = [_frame_cells(*first)]

    for _ in range(1, n):
        placed = _place_next_frame(bboxes[-1], frame_cell_sets)
        if placed is None:
            return None
        bb, cells = placed
        bboxes.append(bb)
        frame_cell_sets.append(cells)

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Complete a four-corner framed rectangle from one decorated anchor rectangle and its diagonal mate.

    Input structure:
    - The background is the dominant color.
    - Two same-color solid rectangular anchors of the same size sit on opposite
      diagonal corners, with the first anchor above-left of the second.
    - The upper-left anchor has two one-cell-thick vertical control bars to its
      right and two one-cell-thick horizontal control bars below it.

    Rule:
    - Copy the anchor rectangle into the two missing corners of the implied
      larger rectangle.
    - Repeat the right-side control bars horizontally between the left and right
      anchors, using their spacing as the period, and draw the outer top and
      bottom borders in the first right-control color.
    - Repeat the below-side control bars vertically between the top and bottom
      anchors, using the same period, and draw the outer left and right borders
      in the first below-control color.

    Key insight: The small control bars are the first two ticks of two periodic
    frame patterns; the diagonal anchor supplies the opposite corner and the
    missing two anchor copies.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    bg = get_bg(g)
    source, dest, right_controls, below_controls = _find_structure(g, bg)

    sr0, sc0, sr1, sc1 = source["bbox"]
    dr0, dc0, dr1, dc1 = dest["bbox"]
    anchor_color = int(source["color"])
    assert int(dest["color"]) == anchor_color, "anchor colors must match"
    assert bbox_h(source["bbox"]) == bbox_h(dest["bbox"]), "anchor heights must match"
    assert bbox_w(source["bbox"]) == bbox_w(dest["bbox"]), "anchor widths must match"
    assert sr0 > 0 and sc0 > 0, "upper-left anchor must have space for outer frame"
    assert dr1 + 1 < g.shape[0] and dc1 + 1 < g.shape[1], "lower-right anchor must have space for outer frame"

    right_offsets = [int(comp["bbox"][1] - sc1) for comp in right_controls]
    below_offsets = [int(comp["bbox"][0] - sr1) for comp in below_controls]
    assert right_offsets == below_offsets and right_offsets[0] == 1, "control offsets must match from the anchor edge"
    step = int(right_offsets[1] - right_offsets[0])
    assert step > 0, "control bars must be separated"
    period = 2 * step
    assert (dc0 - 1 - sc1 - right_offsets[0]) % period == 0, "right frame must close next to the destination anchor"
    assert (dr0 - 1 - sr1 - below_offsets[0]) % period == 0, "below frame must close next to the destination anchor"

    right_colors = [int(comp["color"]) for comp in right_controls]
    below_colors = [int(comp["color"]) for comp in below_controls]
    out = g.copy()

    _paint_rect(out, bg, sr0, dc0, sr1, dc1, anchor_color)
    _paint_rect(out, bg, dr0, sc0, dr1, sc1, anchor_color)

    first_c = int(sc1 + right_offsets[0])
    last_c = int(dc0 - 1)
    for c in range(first_c, last_c + 1):
        offset = int(c - sc1)
        if (offset - right_offsets[0]) % period == 0:
            color = right_colors[0]
        elif (offset - right_offsets[1]) % period == 0:
            color = right_colors[1]
        else:
            continue
        _paint_rect(out, bg, sr0, c, sr1, c, color)
        _paint_rect(out, bg, dr0, c, dr1, c, color)

    _paint_rect(out, bg, sr0 - 1, first_c, sr0 - 1, last_c, right_colors[0])
    _paint_rect(out, bg, dr1 + 1, first_c, dr1 + 1, last_c, right_colors[0])

    first_r = int(sr1 + below_offsets[0])
    last_r = int(dr0 - 1)
    left_c = int(sc0 - 1)
    right_c = int(dc1 + 1)
    for r in range(first_r, last_r + 1):
        _paint(out, bg, r, left_c, below_colors[0])
        _paint(out, bg, r, right_c, below_colors[0])

        offset = int(r - sr1)
        if (offset - below_offsets[0]) % period == 0:
            _paint_rect(out, bg, r, left_c, r, sc1, below_colors[0])
            _paint_rect(out, bg, r, dc0, r, right_c, below_colors[0])
        elif (offset - below_offsets[1]) % period == 0:
            _paint_rect(out, bg, r, sc0, r, sc1, below_colors[1])
            _paint_rect(out, bg, r, dc0, r, dc1, below_colors[1])

    return out

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Slide each black border rectangle to the opposite border, recoloring its swept stripe orange and leaving the rectangle black at the far edge.

    Input structure
    - The grid contains black rectangular 4-connected masks, each touching exactly one outer border.
    - Grey cells form incidental pattern content; orange is the trail color used when a black mask slides.

    Rule
    - Treat all black rectangles as moving simultaneously.
    - A rectangle touching the top or bottom edge moves vertically to the opposite edge in the same columns.
    - A rectangle touching the left or right edge moves horizontally to the opposite edge in the same rows.
    - Recolor the complete swept row or column stripe to orange, then stamp every destination rectangle in black.

    Key insight
    - Edge contact gives the slide direction; the output is the set of opposite-edge black rectangles plus their orange trails.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    assert g.ndim == 2
    h, w = g.shape
    assert h > 0 and w > 0

    moving = Color.BLACK
    trail = Color.ORANGE
    assert np.any(g == moving), "expected at least one black rectangle"
    assert np.any(g == trail), "expected orange trail color to be present"

    out = g.copy()
    targets: list[BBox] = []
    for coords in components_mask(g == moving, connectivity=4):
        r0, c0, r1, c1 = bbox_coords(coords)
        rect_h = r1 - r0 + 1
        rect_w = c1 - c0 + 1
        assert int(coords.shape[0]) == rect_h * rect_w, "black mask must be a solid rectangle"

        side = _edge_side((r0, c0, r1, c1), g.shape)
        if side == "top":
            out[:, c0 : c1 + 1] = trail
            targets.append((h - rect_h, c0, h - 1, c1))
        elif side == "bottom":
            out[:, c0 : c1 + 1] = trail
            targets.append((0, c0, rect_h - 1, c1))
        elif side == "left":
            out[r0 : r1 + 1, :] = trail
            targets.append((r0, w - rect_w, r1, w - 1))
        else:
            assert side == "right"
            out[r0 : r1 + 1, :] = trail
            targets.append((r0, 0, r1, rect_w - 1))

    for r0, c0, r1, c1 in targets:
        out[r0 : r1 + 1, c0 : c1 + 1] = moving

    return out

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Repeat each 3x3 control-center sprite toward the matching solid rectangle until a copy first overlaps that rectangle.

    Input structure
    - The background is the dominant color.
    - Each sprite is a 3x3 foreground object whose eight border pixels have one color and whose center has a different control color.
    - For every control color, there is exactly one separate solid rectangular object of that color.

    Rule
    - Match each sprite to the unique solid rectangle whose color equals the sprite center.
    - Copy the whole 3x3 sprite in the cardinal direction of that rectangle, stepping by three cells each time.
    - Stop after pasting the first copy whose 3x3 bbox overlaps the rectangle; copied pixels overwrite the rectangle there.

    Key insight
    The center pixel is not the paint color: it is a destination key, while the entire 3x3 sprite is the motif tiled along the straight path.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    assert g.ndim == 2
    h, w = g.shape
    assert h >= 3 and w >= 3

    bg = int(get_bg(g))
    sprites = _find_sprites(g, bg)
    assert sprites, "expected at least one 3x3 control-center sprite"

    out = g.copy()
    for sprite_bbox, patch, center in sprites:
        targets = _solid_rectangles(g, bg, center)
        assert len(targets) == 1, "each control color must have one solid rectangular target"
        target_bbox = targets[0]["bbox"]
        assert not _intersects(sprite_bbox, target_bbox), "sprite and target must start separate"

        dr, dc = _direction_to_target(sprite_bbox, target_bbox)
        r, c = sprite_bbox[0], sprite_bbox[1]

        while True:
            current_bbox = (r, c, r + 2, c + 2)
            assert 0 <= r and r + 3 <= h and 0 <= c and c + 3 <= w
            paste(out, patch, r, c)

            if _intersects(current_bbox, target_bbox):
                break

            r += dr * 3
            c += dc * 3

    return out

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalize the framed input motif into a 5x5 icon and stamp two copies on a 15x15 canvas.

    Input structure
    The input is a rounded rectangular frame: the four corners are the background
    color, and every other outer-border pixel has one frame color. Non-background
    pixels inside that frame are the motif to preserve.

    Rule
    Make a 5x5 version of the rounded frame with a 3x3 interior. Crop the input
    interior motif to its bounding box, center that crop in the 3x3 interior, and
    paste the resulting 5x5 icon at upper-left positions (2, 2) and (8, 8) in a
    15x15 background canvas.

    Key insight
    The variable-size frame is only a carrier; the meaningful object is the
    compact interior motif, which is normalized to the fixed 3x3 icon interior.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    h, w = g.shape
    assert h >= 3 and w >= 3

    corners = (g[0, 0], g[0, w - 1], g[h - 1, 0], g[h - 1, w - 1])
    assert len(set(map(int, corners))) == 1
    bg = int(corners[0])

    border = np.concatenate((g[0, :], g[h - 1, :], g[:, 0], g[:, w - 1]))
    frame_colors = set(map(int, border)) - {bg}
    assert len(frame_colors) == 1
    (frame_color,) = tuple(frame_colors)

    assert np.all(g[0, 1 : w - 1] == frame_color)
    assert np.all(g[h - 1, 1 : w - 1] == frame_color)
    assert np.all(g[1 : h - 1, 0] == frame_color)
    assert np.all(g[1 : h - 1, w - 1] == frame_color)

    icon = np.full((5, 5), bg, dtype=int)
    icon[0, 1:4] = frame_color
    icon[4, 1:4] = frame_color
    icon[1:4, 0] = frame_color
    icon[1:4, 4] = frame_color

    interior = g[1 : h - 1, 1 : w - 1]
    motif_box = bbox(interior != bg)
    assert motif_box is not None
    r0, c0, r1, c1 = motif_box
    motif = interior[r0 : r1 + 1, c0 : c1 + 1]
    mh, mw = motif.shape
    assert mh <= 3 and mw <= 3

    icon_r = 1 + (3 - mh) // 2
    icon_c = 1 + (3 - mw) // 2
    icon[icon_r : icon_r + mh, icon_c : icon_c + mw] = motif

    out = np.full((15, 15), bg, dtype=int)
    out[2:7, 2:7] = icon
    out[8:13, 8:13] = icon
    return out

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Convert a rough nested line drawing into a clean canonical frame-and-dot diagram.

    Input structure:
    - The grid has one background color and one foreground color.
    - Foreground 4-connected objects are rough closed frames or small filled blobs.
    - Frames may contain other frames/blobs; blobs outside a frame remain outside it.

    Rule:
    - Detect the containment tree of foreground objects using holes of each frame object.
    - Replace every blob with one foreground pixel.
    - Replace every frame with a rectangular border padded two cells around its direct children.
    - Place siblings by their original row/column overlap and order, with one empty cell between canonical objects.

    Key insight: The exact wobbly geometry is irrelevant; only enclosure plus relative sibling positions define the output.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    bg = int(get_bg(g))
    fg_colors = sorted(set(map(int, g.flatten())) - {bg})
    assert len(fg_colors) == 1
    fg = int(fg_colors[0])

    comps = find_components(g, bg=bg, connectivity=4, monochromatic=True, colors=[fg], return_format="dict")
    assert comps

    nodes: list[_Node] = []
    holes: list[list[np.ndarray]] = []
    for comp in comps:
        coords = np.asarray(comp["coords"], dtype=int)
        node = _Node(
            coords=coords,
            bbox=tuple(map(int, comp["bbox"])),
            center=coords.mean(axis=0),
        )
        node_holes = _component_holes(g.shape, coords)
        node.is_frame = bool(node_holes)
        nodes.append(node)
        holes.append(node_holes)

    assert any(node.is_frame for node in nodes)
    for node_i, node in enumerate(nodes):
        containers = []
        for frame_i, frame in enumerate(nodes):
            if node_i == frame_i or not frame.is_frame:
                continue
            if any(np.all(hole[tuple(node.coords.T)]) for hole in holes[frame_i]):
                containers.append(frame)
        if containers:
            node.parent = min(containers, key=lambda item: int(item.coords.shape[0]))
            node.parent.children.append(node)

    roots = [node for node in nodes if node.parent is None]
    mask = _layout_root(roots)
    out = np.full(mask.shape, bg, dtype=int)
    out[mask] = fg
    return out

def _loop_ok(mask):
    """Check that mask is a single 4-connected simple closed curve with exactly one hole."""
    _, n = label_mask(mask, connectivity=4)
    if n != 1:
        return False
    # Vectorized degree check: each True pixel must have exactly 2 True 4-neighbors
    deg = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=int)
    deg[1:, :] += mask[:-1, :]

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Convert each colored partitioned frame into a horizontal bar whose length is its number of enclosed regions.

    Input structure:
    - Black background with several axis-aligned colored line drawings.
    - The line drawings are damaged by scattered pixels of one non-background noise color and by overlaps with other drawings.
    - Each real drawing is a rectangular partitioned frame enclosing one or more background regions.

    Rule:
    - For each non-background color, reconstruct its horizontal and vertical wall segments from dense row/column evidence.
    - Count the 4-connected background regions fully enclosed by those reconstructed walls.
    - The color with no enclosed region is the noise/pad color.
    - Sort drawing colors by enclosed-region count; equal counts are ordered by which reconstructed frame covers the other.

    Key insight:
    - The scattered color is not an object; it only pads the histogram, while each true object's room count is stable after rectilinear wall reconstruction.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    bg = int(get_bg(g))
    assert bg == 0

    counts: list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray]] = []
    for color in colors_present(g, exclude={bg}):
        rooms = _room_count_for_color(g, int(color))
        walls = _walls_for_color(g, int(color))
        counts.append((int(color), int(rooms), walls))

    drawings = [(color, rooms, walls) for color, rooms, walls in counts if rooms > 0]
    pad_colors = [color for color, rooms, _walls in counts if rooms == 0]
    assert drawings
    assert len(pad_colors) == 1

    pad = int(pad_colors[0])
    ordered: list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray]] = []
    for rooms in sorted({rooms for _color, rooms, _walls in drawings}):
        group = [item for item in drawings if item[1] == rooms]
        ordered.extend(_cover_order(g, group))

    width = max(rooms for _color, rooms, _walls in ordered)

    out = np.full((len(ordered), width), pad, dtype=int)
    for r, (color, rooms, _walls) in enumerate(ordered):
        out[r, :rooms] = int(color)
    return out

_NOISE_FRACTION_RANGE = (0.04, 0.09) # fraction of total cells as noise
_WALL_DAMAGE_FRACTION = 0.25         # max fraction of wall pixels replaced by noise

def _random_gaps(n: int, min_gap: int, max_gap: int, max_total: int) -> list[int] | None:
    """Generate n gaps each in [min_gap, max_gap] with sum <= max_total."""
    if n * min_gap > max_total:
        return None
    gaps = [min_gap] * n
    remaining = max_total - sum(gaps)
    for i in range(n):
        extra = min(max_gap - gaps[i], remaining)
        if extra > 0:
            add = random.randint(0, extra)
            gaps[i] += add
            remaining -= add
    random.shuffle(gaps)
    return gaps


def _build_frame(target_rooms: int, max_h: int = 22, max_w: int = 25) -> np.ndarray | None:
    """Build a boolean wall array with exactly target_rooms enclosed regions."""
    if target_rooms == 1:
        gap_h = random.randint(_CELL_GAP_RANGE[0], max(_CELL_GAP_RANGE[0], max_h - 2))
        gap_w = random.randint(_CELL_GAP_RANGE[0], max(_CELL_GAP_RANGE[0], max_w - 2))
        h, w = gap_h + 2, gap_w + 2
        walls = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
        walls[0, :] = True
        walls[h - 1, :] = True
        walls[:, 0] = True
        walls[:, w - 1] = True
        return walls

    # For target_rooms >= 2: grid of cells, then selectively merge
    possible_configs = []
    for nv in range(2, 6):
        for nh in range(2, 5):
            cells = (nv - 1) * (nh - 1)
            if target_rooms <= cells <= target_rooms + 4:
                possible_configs.append((nv, nh, cells))
    if not possible_configs:
        for nv in range(2, 7):
            for nh in range(2, 6):
                cells = (nv - 1) * (nh - 1)
                if cells >= target_rooms:
                    possible_configs.append((nv, nh, cells))
    if not possible_configs:
        return None

    n_vcols, n_hrows, total_cells = random.choice(possible_configs)
    n_row_gaps = n_hrows - 1
    n_col_gaps = n_vcols - 1
    min_gap, max_gap = _CELL_GAP_RANGE

    if min_gap * n_row_gaps > max_h - 1 or min_gap * n_col_gaps > max_w - 1:
        return None

    row_gaps = _random_gaps(n_row_gaps, min_gap, max_gap, max_h - 1)
    col_gaps = _random_gaps(n_col_gaps, min_gap, max_gap, max_w - 1)
    if row_gaps is None or col_gaps is None:
        return None

def main(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Expand each sparse color object into a filled rectangular region using its legend-paired fill color.

    Input structure
    A background-color grid has a two-column legend in columns 0 and 1, starting at row 0: each row gives
    a source color in the left column and that source color's fill color in the right column.  Outside the
    legend, the foreground pixels are sparse dot objects whose colors are exactly the legend source colors.

    Rule
    Clear the legend.  For each source color, take the bbox of all of its non-legend dots, expand that bbox
    by one pixel in every direction, and fill background cells inside the expanded rectangle with the paired
    legend fill color while preserving every original non-legend dot.

    Key insight
    The legend order is also the layer order: earlier legend rows are in front, so fill rectangles are painted
    from the last legend row back to the first and higher-priority fills overwrite lower-priority fills.
    """
    g = np.asarray(grid, dtype=int)
    bg = get_bg(g)
    H, W = g.shape
    assert W >= 2, "expected room for a two-column legend"

    pairs = _legend_pairs(g, bg)
    source_colors = {source for source, _fill in pairs}
    assert len(source_colors) == len(pairs), "legend source colors must be unique"

    legend_mask = np.zeros(g.shape, dtype=bool)
    legend_mask[: len(pairs), :2] = True
    dot_mask = (g != bg) & ~legend_mask
    assert dot_mask.any(), "expected source dots outside the legend"
    assert set(map(int, g[dot_mask])).issubset(source_colors), "outside dots must use legend source colors"

    dots_by_color: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
    all_dots = np.zeros(g.shape, dtype=bool)
    for source, _fill in pairs:
        coords = np.argwhere(dot_mask & (g == source))
        assert coords.size, "each legend source color must appear outside the legend"
        dots_by_color[source] = coords
        all_dots[coords[:, 0], coords[:, 1]] = True

    out = np.full_like(g, bg)
    for source, fill in reversed(pairs):
        r0, c0, r1, c1 = bbox_coords(dots_by_color[source])
        r0 = max(0, r0 - 1)
        c0 = max(0, c0 - 1)
        r1 = min(H - 1, r1 + 1)
        c1 = min(W - 1, c1 + 1)

        region = out[r0 : r1 + 1, c0 : c1 + 1]
        background_inside_region = ~all_dots[r0 : r1 + 1, c0 : c1 + 1]
        region[background_inside_region] = fill

    out[all_dots] = g[all_dots]
    return out
